title: Web UI: rewrite auto-read as a 1s DOM-polling observer (fixes every-other-article miss; removes fragile afterSwap arm/cancel)
description:
BUG + REWRITE (web UI — packages/aggregator-web/, HTMX + Alpine.js; NOT the TUI)
The auto-read dwell feature (WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS, default 5s) marks only every OTHER article read when navigating consecutively (feed views; reproduced on the Pi). Deterministic alternation from the first article: 1st fails, 2nd fires, 3rd fails, 4th fires...

EVIDENCE (from runtime instrumentation)
- htmx event log: every article open produces exactly one "get /article/{id} -> #reader-content" afterSwap; no visibility events; nothing occurs between a failing article's open and the next open. The auto-read POST (POST /article/{id}/read) appears ~5s after open ONLY for the firing (alternate) articles.
- setTimeout/clearTimeout instrumentation: consecutive opens produced only 3 "SET ms=5050" events and ZERO "CLEAR" events. Conclusion: failing articles NEVER get a dwell timer armed (no setTimeout), and nothing is being cancelled. The current htmx:afterSwap handler (static/app.js ~line 93) is taking a non-arming branch (querySelector('#article-detail') missing, or is-read/no-id -> _dwell.cancel() with nothing pending) on alternate loads. The exact transient-DOM reason at swap time was not pinned down, and the event-driven arm/cancel design has proven too fragile (two prior surgical fixes did not fully resolve it).

DECISION: REPLACE the event-driven arm/cancel machinery entirely with a DOM-polling observer that has no swap-timing dependency.

REMOVE (in static/app.js)
- The entire _dwell IIFE module (currently ~lines 11-87: _timerId/_articleId/_targetMs/_accumulated/_visibleSince, _schedule/_onTimer/_fire/arm/cancel and its visibilitychange listener).
- The global document.addEventListener('htmx:afterSwap', ...) dwell listener (currently ~lines 93-102) that arms/cancels based on the swapped DOM.
- The now-unnecessary _dwell.cancel() calls in the manual paths: _toggleOpenArticleRead (~line 165), _markReadAndNext (~line 179), closeReader (~line 190). (The observer no longer needs them; keep the rest of those functions unchanged.)

ADD: a single once-per-second observer (module-level, runs for the life of the page)
Behavior each tick (setInterval ~1000ms):
1. seconds = parseInt(document.body.dataset.autoReadSeconds || '0', 10). If seconds <= 0 -> reset tracking and return (feature disabled).
2. Determine the currently-dwelt article:
   - The reader must be OPEN: document.body.classList.contains('reader-open') must be true.
   - detail = document.querySelector('#reader-content #article-detail').
   - It counts only if: detail exists AND NOT detail.classList.contains('is-read') AND detail.dataset.articleId is present AND NOT document.hidden.
   - If any condition fails, set lastTick = now, and do NOT accumulate this tick (but keep the current id tracking so re-showing resumes correctly). Return.
3. id = detail.dataset.articleId. If id !== trackedId: reset trackedId = id, visibleMs = 0, lastTick = now, return (start counting fresh for the newly-shown article).
4. Same id and countable: visibleMs += Math.min(now - lastTick, 2000); lastTick = now.  (The 2000ms per-tick cap prevents a throttled/background interval from over-counting a large time gap.)
5. If visibleMs >= seconds*1000 AND id not already in the fired Set: add id to fired Set; fire the read POST using the SAME htmx call the manual path uses:
       htmx.ajax('POST', '/article/' + id + '/read', { target: '#article-detail', swap: 'outerHTML' });
   (target #article-detail so the route returns the refreshed detail + OOB card + HX-Trigger refreshSidebar, keeping all read indicators live.)

STATE (module-level): trackedId (string|null), visibleMs (number), lastTick (number = Date.now()), fired (Set of article-id strings).

REQUIREMENTS / EDGE CASES
- Fire EXACTLY ONCE per article id (the fired Set). This also prevents re-firing in the ~100ms between firing and the is-read swap landing, and prevents auto-re-marking if the user manually un-reads an article we already auto-read.
- Closing the reader (body loses 'reader-open') must stop counting (condition 2) so a closed-but-still-in-DOM detail is never auto-marked.
- Tab hidden (document.hidden) must not accumulate; only visible dwell counts. Do not count large gaps (2000ms per-tick cap).
- Works for BOTH feed articles and thread-member articles (both render #article-detail into #reader-content). Briefs have no #article-detail so are naturally excluded.
- WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS=0 fully disables (no POSTs, ideally the interval is a no-op).
- Do NOT change manual m (toggle read/unread), n (mark read + next), v, c, j/k, or any other behavior. This change is limited to how/when auto-read fires.
- Fire timing granularity of ~1s is acceptable (marks read at roughly seconds..seconds+1s of visible dwell).

REGRESSION / VERIFICATION
- Automated coverage is limited (client-side JS, no browser test harness). Keep/adjust any existing config test for WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS default=5 and the value being surfaced to the page (body data attribute). If a lightweight assertion on the presence of the observer/config wiring is feasible, add it; otherwise document browser verification.
- BROWSER VERIFICATION (state in handoff): in an unread feed, open 5-6 articles CONSECUTIVELY, waiting ~5s on each, navigating with j (and separately with n) -> EVERY article must auto-mark read (no every-other/every-third gap); read indicator on the card + sidebar count update live. Also: opening and closing within <5s -> stays unread; switching tabs mid-dwell -> only visible time counts; auto-read works on thread-member articles; WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS=0 disables; manual m/n still work and are not double-fired by the observer.

FILES: packages/aggregator-web/src/aggregator_web/static/app.js (remove _dwell IIFE + afterSwap dwell listener + the three _dwell.cancel() calls; add the setInterval observer). No backend/model/route/template changes needed (WEB_AUTO_READ_SECONDS already surfaced on body dataset).
